UK man builds WWII-style bunker under garden with 35ft tunnel and beer lift
description: Dave Billings, a fabricator from Derbyshire, has dedicated 11 years to creating an underground garden project. His construction includes two bunkers connected by a long passage, which was inspired by World War II escape tunnels. Billings designed a lift disguised as a beer keg to facilitate drink delivery underground. He plans to connect the bunkers to his home through a concealed entrance leading to an old well.

title: Texas man put $12,000 down on 10 acres; glamping grosses over $100,000 yearly
description: Garrett Brown launched Cameron Ranch Glamping on a picturesque 10-acre plot in Houston, beginning with a minimal budget. He cleverly applied land hacking methods that streamlined utility connections while steering clear of complicated planning processes. The business flourished initially with a geodome, later evolving through zero-cost revenue-sharing arrangements. Rather than relying on third-party bookings, he focused on direct guest engagement, chronicling his experiences in his book, The Glamping Investor.

Francine Lee Lankford claims the property was her permanent home and legally protected from such a sale. On October 21, 2026, an appeals court ruled that her claim required further examination, but did not restore her ownership.

title: BrahMos goes global, eyes next-gen missile by 2028; 1,500-km strike variant on radar
description: BrahMos Aerospace is set to develop the next-generation BrahMos-NG missile by 2027-28. The company aims to strengthen its supply chain and production capacity to meet increasing demand. Interest from foreign militaries in air-launched versions of BrahMos is growing. A 1,500-km-range variant is also under exploration but remains at a conceptual stage. Recent contracts with the Indian Navy are expected to boost domestic manufacturing and participation from local industries.

title: Netanyahu invites PM Modi to light Independence Day torch, hails decades-old ties
Connecticut wool mill that lost 85 jobs now employs 50, makes military fabric
description: A Connecticut wool mill that closed in 2013, leaving 85 workers jobless, has been revived by former investment banker Jacob Harrison Long. He bought the 475,000-square-foot factory in 2014 despite having no manufacturing experience. Twelve years later, the mill employs about 50 people and supplies fabric for US military uniforms. Long now hopes to expand textile manufacturing across New England.

title: Marine life on the brink? 96% of coral reefs could face collapse by 2075
description: The International Union for Conservation of Nature recently highlighted the alarming vulnerability of coral reefs, predicting that by 2075, nearly all shallow-water coral systems may collapse due to rising ocean temperatures. This impending crisis threatens not only marine biodiversity but also the local communities that depend on these ecosystems for their livelihoods.

title: Asian Para Games: Where India stands in medal tally after best day with 7 golds
description: India showcased an extraordinary performance at the Asian Para Games 2026, clinching 26 medals and securing a commendable fourth place overall. With a breathtaking total of 88 medals, including 21 gold, the day was especially memorable for armless archer Sheetal Devi, who bagged two golds in quick succession. Para-athletics was pivotal in this achievement, propelling India past South Korea in the medal standings.

title: Newton's 1687 book on gravity, funded by Halley, sold for Rs 5.49 crore
description: In a significant auction event, a first edition of Isaac Newton's *Philosophiæ naturalis principia mathematica* garnered an impressive US$576,000. This pivotal work introduced revolutionary concepts of motion and gravity through mathematical frameworks. With ties to distinguished scholars like the Kennet family and the vital endorsement from Edmond Halley, Newton's insights continue to resonate in disciplines such as engineering and astronomy, shaping modern scientific thought.

title: Bengaluru horror: Man kills wife, steals motorcycle to dump body in drain Do
description: Mohammad Irfaj, a 22-year-old migrant labourer from Bihar, allegedly murdered his 25-year-old wife Ruksana over infidelity suspicions. The couple’s relationship had deteriorated, leading to frequent quarrels about her phone conversations. On October 10, Irfaj killed Ruksana with a stone and concealed her body in a stormwater drain. Police discovered her body three days later and identified her after public inquiries.

title: Joe Root creates history! Becomes 1st England batter to cross 8,000-run mark in ODIs
description: Joe Root achieved a significant milestone by becoming the first English batter to surpass 8,000 runs in ODIs. This achievement occurred during a match against Sri Lanka in the Pakistan ODI Tri-Series. Root scored 69 runs off 66 balls and has reached a career total of 8,005 runs in 197 matches. His records include 20 centuries and 49 half-centuries, highlighting his batting prowess.

title: Iran claims 7 oil tankers damaged in Hormuz, warns strikes if US helps passage
description: Seven oil tankers sustained damage in the Strait of Hormuz as a result of attacks and naval mines. Four of the tankers reportedly caught fire while transferring oil, creating significant challenges. Iranian authorities have warned of potential targeting of US bases if the situation escalates.

Michigan court upholds $85,000 and $91,250 awards in neighbours' water feud
description: A years-long dispute between neighbours in Michigan over flooding and water flowing across their properties resulted in both sides receiving compensation. A jury awarded $85,000 to William Michael Coan and Cindy Plant and $91,250 to Robert Ercolani. On October 20, 2026, the Michigan Court of Appeals upheld both awards and an independent drainage plan intended to address the flooding.

title: Giannis Antetokounmpo reportedly invested $70 million in real estate in 2025
description: Since October 2025, NBA superstar Giannis Antetokounmpo has strategically invested approximately $70 million in various real estate ventures. His family's company, Ante, has facilitated several significant purchases, including apartment complexes in Wisconsin, Brooklyn, and Chicago. Notably, he recently acquired a lavish $13.5 million mansion in Pinecrest, Florida, after joining the Miami Heat. These investments reflect Antetokounmpo's commitment to expanding his financial portfolio beyond basketball income.

title: France unrest: Macron vows ban on 'illegitimate' protests in coming days
description: In response to escalating unrest, French President Emmanuel Macron unveiled plans to prohibit unauthorized protests while ramping up security measures. Following extensive riots and vandalism, authorities brace for further gatherings this weekend. Trade unions and recognized groups will be directed to alternative protest paths to mitigate potential damage, with the initial disturbances rooted in student protests spurring broader demonstrations against rising living costs, just ahead of France's upcoming presidential election.

title: Can a customer buy more than two iPhones at one time: What Apple Store 'warning' says
description: Apple has introduced a purchase cap that limits online customers to two iPhones per transaction. This rule applies to all iPhone models currently available on the official website. Buyers can mix and match two different devices or purchase two units of the same model. Attempts to add a third phone trigger an explicit warning from the checkout system. This limitation aims to prevent bulk purchases by resellers and scalpers.

title: London duplex in building once home to Keira Knightley lists for £11.5m
description: After an extensive two-year renovation, the Hyde Park Gardens duplex in London stands elegantly restored. Spanning 4,071 square feet, the lavish residence boasts three bedrooms and bathrooms, complemented by a private terrace overlooking four acres of communal greens. Available for £11.5 million, it’s perfect for those craving luxury and convenience, with nearby attractions including Connaught Village and accessible transport at Lancaster Gate and Paddington stations.

title: Russia to review Trump invitation to Putin for G20 summit, possible talks on Ukraine
description: Russia is reviewing the invitation for President Vladimir Putin to attend the upcoming G20 summit in December. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov indicated that no final decision has been made yet. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced Putin's potential attendance could facilitate discussions with various world leaders. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy mentioned the possibility of a trilateral meeting involving Ukraine, Russia, and the United States.

title: Did strategic mistrust prompt Germany to pull out of Boeing's Ghost Bat deal
description: Germany has informed Boeing it will not buy the MQ-28 Ghost Bat drone as it adjusts its plans. The country is looking to acquire F-35 fighter jets while delaying its uncrewed combat aircraft program to early 2030s. Other companies are emerging as competitors, offering alternative drone solutions by 2029. This shift reflects ongoing discussions on military procurement and strategic autonomy amid increasing global security concerns.

title: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes' soccer club value jumps from $275M to $325M
description: Kansas City Current's value increased by 18 percent from $275 million to $325 million in just a year. This valuation places the team second in the National Women's Soccer League, trailing only Angel City FC. The growth in value reflects the stability of the league and solid revenue generation capabilities. Meanwhile, the club continues to work on improving its on-field performance after winning the 2025 Shield.

title: Civil war & terror: Why Libya is still broken 15 yrs after Gaddafi's bloody end
description: Since the fall of Muammar Gaddafi in 2011, Libya has been trapped in a cycle of political strife and disunity. Although a UN-backed agreement was reached with hopes of conducting elections, various administrations maintain control over separate regions. By April 2026, a unified national budget was achieved, yet obstacles to effective implementation loom large.

title: Ralf Schumacher says Lewis Hamilton and Fernando Alonso block young F1 drivers
description: Ralf Schumacher highlighted the issues young drivers face in Formula 1 due to the prolonged careers of veteran racers. He noted that older drivers like Fernando Alonso and Lewis Hamilton are still competitive, which affects opportunities for rising stars. Schumacher stated that if veterans continue racing into their 40s, it may be necessary to reassess the relevance of Formula 2.

title: ‘No permission needed to hoist national flag’: Neha Bora tells Delhi HC
One frame at a time! Story of Multan's Minhas brothers through their father's lens
description: Kashif Minhas once gave up his own cricketing ambitions at his father's insistence. Today, the Multan-based businessman watches his sons Arafat and Sameer represent Pakistan, capturing their journeys through his lens while hoping they will fulfil his dream of winning an ICC trophy for the country.

title: Minnesota court reverses $20,000 privacy award in driveway camera feud
description: In Minnesota, a conflict brewed between two couples over a shared driveway and the removal of a tree. The Stahleys performed maintenance on the Rubys' land without consent, leading to a legal battle. Ultimately, the court awarded the Rubys $27,000, with $20,000 for invasion of privacy. However, the appeals court overturned the privacy ruling, necessitating further proceedings and adjusting the damages for tree removal.

title: 300 gamers raise $1m for cancer research after Oregon woman’s diagnosis
description: When Jessica Conwell confronted the daunting challenge of triple-negative breast cancer, her husband Matt leaned on his gaming community for support. This passionate group rallied together, spearheading fundraising activities that amassed a remarkable $55,000 in their inaugural event. Inspired by early success, they continued their efforts, ultimately raising over $1 million for critical cancer research.

title: Frankfurt’s fitted kitchens turn 100; volunteers save parts from about 50
description: In the year 1926, Margarete Schütte-Lihotzky revolutionized domestic design by creating the Frankfurt Kitchen, aimed at maximizing cooking efficiency for urban dwellers. While around 10,000 of these iconic kitchens were initially integrated into Frankfurt residences, many have since succumbed to renovations. Today, preservationists are dedicated to conserving the remaining kitchens, adapting them with modern appliances while respecting their historical integrity.

title: 'Against policy': Bikaner House on removal of photos from Raihan Vadra exhibition
‘Not change regime, but break country’: BJP says Cong colluding with foreign powers
Why some couples are comfortable with silence, according to psychology
description: Silence in romantic relationships can signal comfort or discomfort based on personal communication styles and emotional needs. The 2024 study revealed that chosen silence often indicates emotional security and closeness. Alternatively, silence resulting from anxiety or hostility may lead to misunderstandings and emotional distance. Understanding each other's preferences regarding conversation and quiet time can strengthen relationships. Ultimately, intimacy is shaped by both meaningful conversations and moments of peaceful silence.

title: Houthis claim Saudi Arabia targeted boat carrying 14 Indians; launch rescue ops
Virginia teen's model improves simulated earthquake sensor coverage by 16.7%
description: A 14-year-old student from Williamsburg, Virginia, has become one of 30 finalists in a national science competition after developing a mathematical model to improve earthquake sensor placement. Isabel Rossi's six-month research project showed that adding just five sensors could increase simulated detection coverage by 16.7%. She used earthquake records from California and mathematical methods to identify better sensor locations.

title: After renaming Lake Ontario, Google CEO rejects US request to rename Atlantic Ocean
description: President Trump has recently proposed renaming the Atlantic Ocean, following prior discussions about the Atlantic Ocean. During a recent event, he mentioned contacting Google Maps regarding these renaming efforts. Google CEO Sundar Pichai reportedly declined his proposal on the grounds that oceans encompass multiple countries. This follows the US administration's earlier renaming of Lake Ontario to Lake America for US users.

title: Georgia woman loses marijuana smoke case as court upholds pension fund immunity
description: A Georgia woman sued after claiming her neighbour’s marijuana smoke repeatedly entered her apartment despite a no-smoking lease, affecting her breathing and health. Bridget Francis alleged that the apartment management ignored her complaints. However, on October 19, 2026, a Georgia appeals court upheld the dismissal of her claims against a California teachers’ pension fund, ruling that it was legally protected from the lawsuit.

title: Maldives begins planting coral on 2 submerged planes to build artificial reef
description: Two decommissioned Dornier 228 aircraft are submerged near Kudagiri Island to create a diving attraction. Conservation teams are working to establish an artificial reef by attaching coral fragments to underwater frames. The project aims to combine marine tourism with aviation history while promoting coral growth. Various organizations are collaborating to monitor the ecological impact of this initiative.

title: 3 aircraft carriers, jets & troops: Israel, US plan to attack Iran after midterms
description: The United States and Israel are preparing for potential military strikes against Iran after the upcoming midterm elections. Iran has announced it will reveal a new weapon called the 'Father of All Bombs' as tensions rise. US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth met Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to discuss military options recently. Meanwhile, Iranian officials warn of severe responses if attacked, emphasizing improved missile capabilities.

title: What El Nino? This ground up farmers’ cooperative continues to reap dividends
description: Farmers in Mulkanoor village have established a cooperative that supports agricultural needs, improving self-reliance. This cooperative has recently partnered with HarvestLink to export branded rice to the US market. They expect their first shipment of rice to be dispatched within a month, pending regulations. The cooperative has a strong membership base and provides various support services to its members.

title: Florida couple missed 66 mortgage payments; man's bank lawsuit rejected
description: A Florida couple missed 66 monthly mortgage payments on their Naples property, triggering a foreclosure dispute that began in 2009. During the legal battle, Gregory Brian Myers agreed to deposit $5,000 monthly while appealing the foreclosure. He later sued U.S. Bank, alleging it had violated their agreement. On October 19, 2026, a federal appeals court upheld the dismissal of his lawsuit.
